text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- NATO will continue to see the Baltic states as candidates for the alliance, NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said at the historic Madrid summit when the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland were invited to join the alliance.

- A report in the Financial Times that the European Union was prepared to invite Estonia in a first round of enlargement was received with positive comments in Latvia but with dissastisfaction in Lithuania.
- More than 200 cultural figures signed a declaration asking for explanations from the interior ministry over the murder of actor Sulev Luik and more police patrols on the streets.
- 23 representatives from China's 11 largest companies started a three-day visit to Estonia.
- The government heard a report by the transport and communications ministry on plans to sell a 30 percent stake in Eesti Telekom.
- Customs guards in the eastern town of Narva found a car with radioactivity over 200 times the normal.
- The immigration department has issued 124,600 passports to aliens, mainly Russian-speakers who do not have citizenship of the country.
- Estonia should pass a law on the Red Cross and protect the use of its symbol, International Committee of the Red Cross head George Weber said during a visit.
- A Baltic-U.S. charter on cooperation may be signed in September, Estonian diplomats said, quoting U.S. officials.
- The Estonian, Latvian and Lithuanian president will meet the Polish, Czech and Hungarian presidents in Madrid. A meeting with U.S. President Bill Clinton will not take place.
- Shares in Hansapank and Hoiupank hit record highs after first-half results. The price of privatisation vouchers rose 8.5 percent.
